title: Parker House Rolls
description: Soft, buttery folded dinner rolls named for Boston's Parker House hotel, as written down by Fannie Farmer. Her Boston Cooking-School Cook Book (1896) popularised level, standardised measurements in American home cooking.
notes:
Parker House Rolls

2 cups scalded milk
3 tablespoons butter
2 tablespoons sugar
1 teaspoon salt
1 yeast cake dissolved in
¼ cup lukewarm water
Flour

Add butter, sugar, and salt to milk; when lukewarm, add dissolved yeast cake and three cups of flour. Beat thoroughly, cover, and let rise until light; cut down, and add enough flour to knead (it will take about two and one-half cups). Let rise again, toss on slightly floured board, knead, pat, and roll out to one-third inch thickness. Shape with biscuit-cutter, first dipped in flour. Dip the handle of a case knife in flour, and with it make a crease through the middle of each piece; brush over one-half of each piece with melted butter, fold, and press edges together. Place in greased pan, one inch apart, cover, let rise, and bake in hot oven twelve to fifteen minutes. As rolls rise they will part slightly, and if hastened in rising are apt to lose their shape.

Fannie Merritt Farmer, *The Boston Cooking-School Cook Book* (Boston: Little, Brown, 1896), Chapter on Bread and Bread Making. Quoted from the 1910 printing on Project Gutenberg (eBook #65061, p. 58); the wording matches the 1896 first edition, pp. 61–62.

Adapted: one yeast cake becomes a packet of active dry yeast, rise times and a "hot oven" are given in modern terms, and the rolls get a final brush of butter.
ingredients: 3 tablespoons unsalted butter, plus 4 tablespoons melted for brushing
5 1/2 cups (about 690 g) all-purpose flour, plus more for the board
steps: Heat the milk in a saucepan until steaming with small bubbles at the edge. Stir in the 3 tablespoons butter, the sugar, and the salt, then cool to lukewarm, about 105°F (40°C).
Sprinkle the yeast over the lukewarm water and let it stand until foamy, about 5 minutes.
Add the yeast and 3 cups of the flour to the milk and beat hard for 2 minutes to make a smooth batter. Cover and let rise until light and bubbly, about 1 hour.
Stir the batter down and add enough of the remaining flour to make a soft dough, about 2 1/2 cups. Knead on a floured board until smooth and elastic, about 8 minutes.
Put the dough in a buttered bowl, cover, and let rise until doubled, 1 to 1 1/2 hours.
Turn the dough out, knead briefly, and roll to 1/3 inch thick. Cut into rounds with a floured 2 1/2-inch cutter.
Press a deep crease across the middle of each round with the floured handle of a knife or wooden spoon. Brush one half with melted butter, fold over, and press the edges together.
Set the rolls 1 inch apart on buttered baking sheets. Cover and let rise until puffy, 30 to 45 minutes. Don't rush this rise or the rolls lose their shape.
Bake at 425°F (220°C) until golden, 12 to 15 minutes. Brush with the remaining melted butter and serve warm.
